why: This week is Trie + DFS, but a path here never branches: it goes straight right (or straight down), may reverse once, and then retraces. A word is fixed by its start cell, its direction and its turn point, so a direct scan over those choices is enough. The allowed complexity is O(rows*cols*words*maxLen).
hints: Reversing means going back the way you came, so after the turn you revisit cells you already used.

A match is a start cell, a direction (right or down) and a turn index t: letters 0..t go forward and letters t+1.. go back from cell t. t = len-1 means no turn. For length >= 2 each match is a distinct path, so count every (start, dir, t) that fits.

For each start and direction, first find how far the word matches going forward (f letters). Each t < f is then a candidate, and you check the remaining letters walking back. Count one-letter words once per cell.
pitfalls: A path may not start leftward or upward. Turning at t = 0 (going back immediately) is not allowed.
A one-letter word matches both 'directions' at the same cell, but it is a single occurrence.
Count occurrences, not distinct words: 'ac' appears 3 times in the example.
statement:
You are given a character grid and a list of distinct words (phrases). Count how many times words can be found in the grid, where a word is found along a path of adjacent cells such that:

  • the path starts at any cell and first goes left to right or top to bottom;
  • it may change direction once to the opposite direction (right→left, or down→up), walking back over the cells it came from.

Each different path spelling a word counts once.

Example: grid

a b a c
x a c d
y r d s

with words [ac, cat, car, bar, acdc, abacaba] gives 7:

  • ac 3 times: (1,1)→(1,2) right, (0,2)→(0,3) right, (0,2)→(1,2) down.
  • bar once: (0,1)→(1,1)→(2,1) down.
  • acdc twice: a(1,1) c(1,2) d(1,3), then back to c(1,2); and a(0,2) c(1,2) d(2,2), then back up to c(1,2).
  • abacaba once: right along row 0 to c(0,3), then back to a(0,0).
  • cat and car are not found. 3+1+2+1 = 7.

The source allows time complexity up to O(rows × cols × words × maxWordLength).
constraints: • Not stated in the source. Assume 1 ≤ rows, cols ≤ 100, 1 ≤ words.length ≤ 100, 1 ≤ words[i].length ≤ 100, distinct words, lowercase letters only.
